issues.legal_issue: Notifications initiating and declaring a land acquisition are not encumbrances affecting property that are removed when the property vests under the nationalisation law.
material_facts: The State issued notifications under the land acquisition law to acquire land belonging to a textile undertaking for a public purpose.

While a challenge to the notifications was pending, the textile undertaking vested in the Central Government and was then transferred to the National Textile Corporation under the nationalisation law.
The National Textile Corporation argued that the notifications were encumbrances and therefore became ineffective upon vesting.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition notifications were not encumbrances within the meaning of the nationalisation law and did not become inoperative when the land vested in the Central Government.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 4(1)–(2) of the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974, property vests in the Central Government and is freed from trusts, obligations, mortgages, charges, liens and other encumbrances; specified attachments, injunctions, decrees and court orders restricting use are separately deemed withdrawn. “Encumbrance” means a claim, lien or liability attached to property, such as a burden that runs with the land, and is read in the context of the listed burdens. The separate treatment of court restrictions indicates that “encumbrance” does not mean every kind of fetter on property. A State’s sovereign power to acquire land is paramount to, and outside, ownership of the land (The Collector of Bombay v. Nusserwanji Rattanji Mistri, [1955] 1 SCR 1311).

predicates.nationalisation_vesting_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a land acquisition notification ceased to operate when property vested under a law transferring an undertaking to the State.
predicates.property_vested_in_state: The undertaking’s property vested in the State under a law transferring the undertaking.
predicates.state_issued_land_acquisition_notificati: The State issued notifications to acquire land belonging to the undertaking.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns the effect of vesting an undertaking’s property in the State and the State had issued acquisition notifications for its land, those notifications remain effective after vesting.
